name: charAt()
description: Returns the character at the specified index in a string.
parameters: index — zero-based position of the character to return (default 0).
returns: A single-character string, or an empty string if the index is out of range.
notes: Bracket notation ('hello'[1]) does the same thing and is more commonly used today.

name: charCodeAt()
description: Returns the UTF-16 numeric code of the character at the given index.
parameters: index — zero-based position of the character (default 0).
returns: A number representing the UTF-16 code unit, or NaN if out of range.
notes: Use String.fromCharCode() to go the other direction, from code to character.

name: String.at()
description: Returns the character at the given index, supporting negative indices to count from the end of the string.
parameters: index — position to access; negative values count backward from the end.
returns: A single-character string, or undefined if out of range.
notes: Also available on arrays as array.at(index).

name: String.indexOf()
description: Returns the index of the first occurrence of a substring within the string, or -1 if not found.
parameters: searchValue — substring to search for. fromIndex — optional index to start searching from.
returns: The index of the first match, or -1.

name: String.lastIndexOf()
description: Returns the index of the last occurrence of a substring, searching the string backwards.
parameters: searchValue — substring to search for. fromIndex — optional index to start searching backward from.
returns: The index of the last match, or -1 if not found.

name: String.includes()
description: Determines whether one string may be found within another, returning true or false.
parameters: searchValue — substring to search for. fromIndex — optional index to start searching from.
returns: Boolean indicating whether the substring was found.
notes: Case-sensitive — normalize casing with toLowerCase() first if needed.

name: startsWith()
description: Determines whether a string begins with the characters of a specified substring.
parameters: searchValue — substring to check for. position — optional index to start checking from.
returns: Boolean indicating whether the string starts with searchValue.

name: endsWith()
description: Determines whether a string ends with the characters of a specified substring.
parameters: searchValue — substring to check for. endPosition — optional index treated as the end of the string.
returns: Boolean indicating whether the string ends with searchValue.

name: String.slice()
description: Extracts a section of a string and returns it as a new string, without modifying the original.
parameters: start — index to begin extraction. end — index to stop before (exclusive).
returns: A new string containing the extracted section.
notes: Supports negative indices, which count from the end of the string — unlike substring().

name: substring()
description: Returns the part of the string between two indices, similar to slice() but without negative index support.
parameters: start — index to begin extraction. end — index to stop before (exclusive).
returns: A new string containing the extracted section.
notes: Negative or swapped arguments are automatically clamped/swapped, unlike slice().

name: split()
description: Splits a string into an array of substrings based on a specified separator.
parameters: separator — string or regex to split on. limit — optional maximum number of pieces to include.
returns: An array of substrings.
notes: Passing an empty string splits into individual characters.

name: trim()
description: Removes whitespace from both ends of a string, without affecting the original string.
returns: A new string with leading and trailing whitespace removed.

name: trimStart()
description: Removes whitespace from the beginning of a string only.
returns: A new string with leading whitespace removed.

name: trimEnd()
description: Removes whitespace from the end of a string only.
returns: A new string with trailing whitespace removed.

name: toUpperCase()
description: Converts a string to upper case, returning a new string.
returns: A new upper-cased string.

name: toLowerCase()
description: Converts a string to lower case, returning a new string.
returns: A new lower-cased string.

name: replace()
description: Returns a new string with the first match of a pattern replaced by a given replacement.
parameters: pattern — string or regex to match. replacement — string or function producing the replacement.
returns: A new string with the replacement applied.
notes: Only replaces the first match unless a global regex (/pattern/g) is used.

name: replaceAll()
description: Returns a new string with all matches of a pattern replaced by a given replacement.
parameters: pattern — string or global regex to match. replacement — string or function producing the replacement.
returns: A new string with all replacements applied.
notes: A non-global regex pattern throws a TypeError — use the /g flag or a string pattern.

name: repeat()
description: Constructs and returns a new string containing the specified number of copies of the original string.
parameters: count — number of times to repeat, must be a non-negative integer.
returns: A new, repeated string.
notes: Throws a RangeError for negative or infinite counts.

name: padStart()
description: Pads the current string from the start with a given string until it reaches the target length.
parameters: targetLength — desired total length. padString — string to pad with (default is a space).
returns: A new, padded string.
notes: Commonly used for zero-padding numbers or aligning output.

name: padEnd()
description: Pads the current string from the end with a given string until it reaches the target length.
parameters: targetLength — desired total length. padString — string to pad with (default is a space).
returns: A new, padded string.

name: String.concat()
description: Combines the text of one or more strings and returns a new string.
returns: A new string combining all inputs.
notes: Template literals or the + operator are generally preferred over concat() in modern code.
